facts.fact_text: The applicant is a member of the Human Rights Association in Turkey.
At 8 p.m. on 8 April 2002, around 30-35 persons gathered at Tünel Square holding candles, photos and banners.
The banners held by the demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 stated, inter alia, "All the world is Palestine, all of us are Palestinians".
The banners held by the demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 stated, inter alia, "an end to the occupation, freedom to Palestine".
The banners held by the demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 stated, inter alia, "Wanted Ariel Sharon war-criminal".
The demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 sat down on the street.

The applicant submitted in the application form that on 8 April 2002 he had arrived at Tünel Square in order to participate in the Human Rights Association's press release on Israel's invasion of Palestine.
The police chief warned the demonstrators many times to disperse on 8 April 2002 at Tünel Square.
The police used force to arrest the two persons, including the applicant, who continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.
The applicant submitted that the police then arrested him and Ms M.A.
The applicant and Ms M.A. were brought to the Beyoğlu police station following their arrest on 8 April 2002.
The applicant and Ms M.A. were released from the Beyoğlu police station 1.5 hours after their arrest on 8 April 2002.
The Beyoğlu public prosecutor considered in his decision of 7 August 2003 that the force used by the security forces was in line with Article 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
A description of the relevant domestic law at the material time can be found in Mehmet Ümit Erdem v. Turkey, no. 42234/02, § 19, 17 July 2008.

According to official police documents drafted on 8 April 2002 at 9.15 p.m., the security forces received information that the Human Rights Association would hold an unauthorised demonstration and press release concerning Israel's operations against Palestine at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.

According to official police documents drafted on 8 April 2002 at 9.30 p.m., the security forces received information that the Human Rights Association would hold an unauthorised demonstration and press release concerning Israel's operations against Palestine at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.

In his decision of 7 August 2003, the Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that about 30-35 persons had gathered with candles and banners at Tünel in Beyoğlu on 8 April 2002 in order to protest Israel's invasion of Palestine.
At 8 p.m. on 8 April 2002, around 30-35 persons gathered at Tünel Square holding candles, photos and banners.
The demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 sat down on the street.
The group of demonstrators at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 started to disperse.
Two persons, including the applicant, continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002 despite warnings from the police.
The police used force to arrest the two persons, including the applicant, who continued to sit and shout slogans at Tünel Square on 8 April 2002.
The applicant submitted that the police chief and 5 or 6 other police officers beat him up.
The applicant claimed to have received punches and kicks during his arrest on 8 April 2002.
The applicant claimed to have been hit by a truncheon on various parts of his body, including his head and his back, during his arrest on 8 April 2002.
The doctor who examined the applicant at Taksim Hospital noted a swelling and ecchymosis of 2 cm on the applicant's head in the frontal region.
The doctor at the Beyoğlu Forensic Medicine Department noted a swelling of 2 cm on the applicant's head in the frontal region on 9 April 2002.

In his decision of 7 August 2003, the Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that the complainants had continued to sit down and shout slogans after warnings to disperse on 8 April 2002, and as a result the police had had to use force and arrest them.
